title: Craft Blend 4-Mix Solo #02 (가로 띠·물결)
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph with a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Japanese woman in her early 50s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, a deep bronze tan foundation over real skin, wide stark-white paint bands above and below both eyes lying on the lids and never across the eyeballs, neon pink and turquoise eyeshadow, long false lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, glossy white lips, small star and heart rhinestone stickers on the cheeks only, a bold cheeky grin, cheerful, cool ash-brown hair styled in tight zigzag crimped waves, real living eyes. Long coffin nails, matte finish.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. Huge rounded shoulders and thick, powerfully muscular arms with the swell of the muscle visible beneath a soft layer, a colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size. Below that waistline a great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and drops down under its own weight, gathering into two or three heavy rounded folds, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline, colossal thighs with a muscular sweep visible beneath the fat, thick heavy calves. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a smooth taut surface with natural creases and shadow only where the flesh folds. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 horizontal bands by 3 hazy transition zones centred about 31% of the way down her figure from the top, about 50% of the way down her figure from the top and about 72% of the way down her figure from the top. Region 1 is everything above the first transition zone: it is painted in Swedish Dalarna kurbits folk painting (a deep barn-red ground with bold cream and gold curling scrollwork), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense curling floral scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the band between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in American Art Deco chrome-and-lacquer (a deep black lacquer ground with bold silver chrome sunburst), wide silver chrome bands following the contours of the body, dense zigzag linework filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the band between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Indian Mughal miniature gold-work (a deep midnight-blue ground with fine gold linework and medallions), wide gold-and-crimson bands following the contours of the body, dense jewel-toned scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 4 is everything below the last transition zone: it is painted in Ethiopian cross-and-lattice gold pattern (a deep wine-red ground with fine gold lattice linework), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense lattice linework filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a gently undulating wave, rising and falling softly, rather than a straight course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Pose: mid-stride walking toward camera, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Footwear: extreme platform stiletto Mary Janes, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Background & Lighting: the blended painted patterns reading crisp against her skin, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide. portrait 2:3 vertical.
